The trekker administration is established around Botshabelo and the Vet River. The southern districts will be administered together.
The emigrant communities on the Vet River are joining the southern trekker administration.
The political circumstances that prompted the earlier British demand have changed. The old exchange can no longer determine the present settlement.

Potgieter's followers seek a permanent settlement in the northern district. Local arrangements may recognise their administration around the settlement, although indigenous claims and authority remain contested throughout the wider district.
The northern community can establish its local administration where no other state holds the district.

The northern community requests local administration of its settlement district within the wider emigrant political order. Recognition will preserve the community as a separate district until eventual incorporation.
Ivory, livestock and wagon commerce connect the northern settlement with distant markets. Local traders can support the market without committing the tiny treasury to a great public project.
